support.heroTitle: Cleaner places need more than good intentions.
support.heroP1: Every day, people walk past litter in streets, parks, beaches, hiking paths and neighbourhoods. Most of them care — but reporting it is often slow, unclear or invisible.
support.heroP2: Drosia makes it simple: take a photo, send a report, and help create a public signal that shows where action is needed.
support.heroP3: We want to keep Drosia independent, ad-free and respectful of people's data. That's why we're looking for supporters who share the same goal: cleaner public spaces and more transparent local action.
support.why1Body: Individual complaints often disappear into inboxes. Drosia turns reports into a shared map, making problem areas easier to understand and harder to ignore.
support.why2Title: You support civic action without barriers
support.why2Body: No account. No complicated process. No data selling. Anyone can report a problem in less than a minute.
support.why3Title: You connect your organisation with a visible mission
support.why3Body: Supporting Drosia is a practical way to show that your organisation cares about the places where people live, work, travel and spend time outdoors.
support.whoHotelBody: Clean surroundings are part of the guest experience. Supporting Drosia helps protect the beaches, streets, viewpoints, trails and neighbourhoods that make a destination worth visiting.
support.whoMuniBody: Drosia can help you see where residents are reporting litter, understand recurring hotspots and show that public feedback leads to action.
support.whoNgoBody: Use Drosia as a simple tool for awareness campaigns, clean-up initiatives, local reporting drives and community engagement.
support.howBody: Support doesn't have to mean one fixed package. Depending on your organisation, it could mean helping cover running costs, sharing Drosia with your community, using it in a local campaign, connecting us with municipalities, or supporting reporting in a specific area.
support.howGoal: The goal is simple: help more people report litter easily, and help more places respond.
support.formIntro: Tell us a little about who you are and which places you care about. We'll read your message and get back to you personally.
support.formNote: No pressure. No fixed package. Just a first conversation about cleaner public spaces and how Drosia could help.

sections.p: Drosia works without an account. We don't ask for your name or email, we don't sell data, and we don't track you across the web. You report a problem; we forward it to the responsible authority and show its status publicly.

The photo(s) you send, the location of the problem (from the photo, your device's GPS, or a pin you set), the category, and an optional description. A random device token stored in your browser lets you find your own reports and receive updates — it is not linked to your identity.

Before a photo is shown publicly it is automatically anonymised — faces and vehicle number plates are obscured. Original photos stay private and are only accessible to our moderation for review. Please don't photograph identifiable people or private property.
The anonymised photo, the approximate location, the category and the status are shown on the public map and the report's tracking page, and are forwarded to the responsible public authority.

Hosting and database (Supabase), email delivery to authorities (Resend), hosting and privacy-friendly, cookieless analytics (Vercel), and map tiles and place lookup (OpenStreetMap / Nominatim). Each processes data only to run this service.
Reports and their status are kept as long as they are useful for public accountability. Original (non-anonymised) photos are kept only as long as needed for moderation and abuse prevention.

You can ask us to access or delete a report, or dispute content. Use the "Report / dispute" button on any public report, or contact us. Under the GDPR you also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.

Drosia is a free tool for reporting litter and environmental issues to the responsible public authority. Reports are statements by users, not official findings by an authority.

Only report what you have the right to photograph. Document the problem, not people: no identifiable individuals, and no private property or private persons singled out. Reports that target private individuals are removed.

You keep your rights to your photos and grant Drosia permission to anonymise, display and forward them for the purpose of the service. You confirm your report is truthful to the best of your knowledge.
We review reports before they go public and may reject or remove content that is spam, unlawful, or points at private persons. Anyone can flag content with the "Report / dispute" button.

Drosia is provided "as is". We can't guarantee that an authority will act, or that information is complete or error-free. Accountability figures are based on delivered citizen reports and are not official findings.
